title: Single-cell omics & GWAS integration · Wednesday, November 25

transcript.text: This is the Paper Library daily on Single-cell omics & GWAS integration, for Wednesday, November 25.
Let's turn to single-cell omics and GWAS integration, where today we have one new atlas.

It's a Research Square preprint from the Li lab: a spatially resolved multi-omics atlas of the human optic nerve, part of the Human Cell Atlas. The question is which optic nerve cell types and regulatory programs might carry genetic risk for glaucoma.

It's big: about two point one million nuclei from 108 donors, profiled with single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing plus Xenium spatial transcriptomics. They define ten major cell classes and more than sixty populations, each with its regulatory elements and transcription factor regulons.

They also find spatial gradients along the nerve and trace adult lineages for oligodendroglia and astrocytes. With age, progenitor-like glia and microglia become less abundant, and cell-cycle programs decline.
Then the GWAS part. The authors overlay glaucoma and other neuro-ophthalmic signals on the atlas and report new insights into the cells involved.
That's the part to be careful with, because the abstract doesn't name specific cell types or give enrichment statistics. Treat it as a reference resource first and mechanistic claims second.
Still, chromatin accessibility at this resolution should make fine-mapping glaucoma variants to specific enhancers much more workable.
Takeaway: the optic nerve now has a large, multi-modal, age-aware single-cell reference for mapping glaucoma risk, but the genetic conclusions need checking against the full paper.

papers.title: An Integrated Single-cell Multi-Omics Atlas of the Human Optic Nerve
